issues.description: The solution references the global symbol display_start as the framebuffer base address (used in set_pixel and in main) but the solution repository does not declare or allocate display_start. The template and problem statement expect a global buffer named display_start (the template declares it as 'display_start RESB 8294400'). This mismatch means the solution as provided is not structurally consistent with the template/problem: the referenced symbol is missing, so the solution will not assemble/run and students will be confused about where display_start is defined and whether they should use a global buffer or a local one.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore a consistent definition of display_start so the solution matches the template and problem statement. Options: (a) Reintroduce the global allocation in the solution (e.g. in .bss: 'display_start RESB 8294400') to match the template, or (b) if moving display_start to a local stack scope was intended, update all references in the solution and the problem statement/template to pass the base address explicitly (e.g. via a register or as a parameter) and document that change. The simplest fix is to add 'display_start RESB 8294400' to solution_repository/pixel.asm in the .bss section so the symbol exists and matches the template.
